## Natural history notes

A small crab spider characterized by its elongated pale green body, laterally held legs, and subtle whitish or yellowish markings that help it blend among leaves, stems, and flowers. In Florida, the American Green Crab Spider is found in gardens, fields, roadsides, forest edges, wetlands, shrubs, and other sunny habitats with low vegetation and flowering plants. It is an ambush predator, waiting motionless on foliage or flowers and grabbing visiting flies, bees, moths, and other small insects with its enlarged front legs rather than building a prey-capture web.
